passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Tardigrades are microscopic animals, most about half a millimeter long.
• They live in many habitats, including moss, soil, and ocean sediment.
• When their surroundings dry out, they can enter a state called cryptobiosis.
• In cryptobiosis, a tardigrade's metabolism slows to less than 0.01% of its normal rate.
• Tardigrades in this state have survived for years and revived when water returned.

content.stem: The student wants to explain how tardigrades survive when their surroundings dry out. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tardigrades, most of which are about half a millimeter long, live in moss, soil, and ocean sediment.

choices.label: B
choices.text: When their surroundings dry out, tardigrades enter cryptobiosis, slowing their metabolism to less than 0.01% of its normal rate; in this state, they can survive for years until water returns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tardigrades are microscopic animals that live in many different habitats, including ocean sediment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cryptobiosis is a state that tardigrades are able to enter.

content.explanation: The goal is to explain how tardigrades survive drying out. Choice B says what happens (they enter cryptobiosis), how it works (metabolism slows drastically), and the result (they survive for years and revive).

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This describes the animals' size and habitats but not how they survive drying out.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This describes the animals and their habitats but not how they survive drying out.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This names cryptobiosis but doesn't connect it to drying out or explain how it helps them survive.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The kalimba is a small handheld instrument related to the mbira, a family of African instruments.
• A kalimba has a row of thin metal tines attached to a wooden board or box.
• Kalimba players pluck the tines with their thumbs.
• The marimba is a large percussion instrument with wooden bars arranged like a piano keyboard.
• Marimba players strike the bars with mallets.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in how players make sound on the two instruments. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The kalimba is related to the mbira, a family of African instruments.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The kalimba has thin metal tines attached to a wooden board or box, while the marimba has wooden bars.

choices.label: C
choices.text: While kalimba players pluck metal tines with their thumbs, marimba players strike wooden bars with mallets.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The marimba is a large percussion instrument whose wooden bars are arranged like a piano keyboard.

content.explanation: The goal is to contrast how players make sound on the two instruments. Choice C does this directly: kalimba players pluck tines with their thumbs, while marimba players strike bars with mallets. The word "while" signals the contrast.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This gives background on the kalimba only and says nothing about how either instrument is played.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This contrasts what the instruments are made of, not how players make sound on them.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes only the marimba and doesn't say how it is played.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2021, archaeologist Leila Haddad led an excavation at a site near the village of Korvel.
• Her team uncovered the remains of a bakery about 1,800 years old.
• The bakery contained three large clay ovens.
• Charred remains of wheat and barley were found near the ovens.
• Haddad believes the bakery supplied bread to much of the surrounding settlement.

content.stem: The student wants to indicate when and where Haddad's excavation took place. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In 2021, Leila Haddad led an excavation near the village of Korvel, where her team uncovered an ancient bakery.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leila Haddad's team uncovered a bakery that contained three large clay ovens.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The bakery uncovered by Haddad's team is about 1,800 years old and may have supplied bread to much of its settlement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Charred wheat and barley were found near the ovens of an ancient bakery uncovered by Haddad's team.

content.explanation: The goal asks for when and where the excavation happened. Choice A gives both: in 2021, near the village of Korvel.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This describes what the team found but not when or where the excavation took place.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This gives the age of the bakery, not the year of the excavation, and it doesn't say where the site is.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes evidence found at the site but not when or where the excavation took place.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Biomimicry is the practice of designing products by imitating structures or processes found in nature.
• Swiss engineer George de Mestral noticed burrs clinging to his dog's fur after a walk.
• Burrs are covered with tiny hooks that catch on loops of fur or fabric.
• De Mestral used this hook-and-loop idea to invent Velcro.
• Japanese engineer Eiji Nakatsu redesigned the nose of a high-speed train based on the shape of a kingfisher's beak.

content.stem: The student wants to present the invention of Velcro as an example of biomimicry. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Biomimicry, the practice of imitating nature in design, led Eiji Nakatsu to base a high-speed train's nose on the shape of a kingfisher's beak.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Velcro is an example of biomimicry, the practice of imitating nature in design: George de Mestral based its hooks and loops on burrs that clung to his dog's fur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Swiss engineer George de Mestral noticed burrs clinging to his dog's fur after a walk.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Burrs are covered with tiny hooks that catch on loops of fur or fabric.

content.explanation: The goal has two parts: talk about Velcro and present it as biomimicry. Choice B names biomimicry, defines it, and explains how Velcro imitated burrs, so it does both.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This presents an example of biomimicry, but it is the train, not Velcro.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This describes what inspired de Mestral but doesn't mention Velcro or biomimicry.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes burrs but doesn't mention Velcro or biomimicry.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Psychologist Hana Mori studied 60 college students learning a list of words.
• Students who slept for eight hours after learning the list recalled more words the next day than students who stayed awake.
• Neuroscientist Daniel Reyes studied 45 adults learning a short piano melody.
• Participants who took a 90-minute nap after practicing played the melody more accurately later than those who did not nap.
• Mori's study tested memory for words, while Reyes's tested memory for a physical skill.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the findings of the two studies. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mori's study tested memory for words, while Reyes's study tested memory for a physical skill.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Mori studied 60 college students, and Reyes studied 45 adults.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reyes found that adults who napped for 90 minutes after practicing a melody later played it more accurately than those who did not nap.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In both Mori's and Reyes's studies, participants who slept after learning something performed better later than those who did not sleep.

content.explanation: The goal is to stress what the two studies found in common. Choice D states the shared result: in both studies, sleeping after learning led to better performance later.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This points out a difference between the studies, not a similarity.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This describes who took part in each study, not what either study found.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This reports the finding of only one study, so it can't show a similarity between them.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Rammed earth walls are made by packing damp soil, sand, and clay into a frame and compacting it in layers.
• The finished walls are thick and dense.
• Thick, dense walls absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night.
• This can reduce a building's need for heating and air conditioning.
• Building with rammed earth takes a lot of labor and can cost more than building with wood framing.
• Architect Sofia Varga used rammed earth walls for a school she designed in a desert region in 2022.

content.stem: The student wants to explain why rammed earth walls can lower a building's energy use. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rammed earth walls are made by packing damp soil, sand, and clay into a frame and compacting it in layers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Although rammed earth walls can reduce the need for heating and air conditioning, they take a lot of labor and can cost more than wood framing.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Because rammed earth walls are thick and dense, they absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night, which can reduce the need for heating and air conditioning.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2022, architect Sofia Varga used rammed earth walls for a school she designed in a desert region.

content.explanation: The goal is to explain why the walls can save energy. Choice C gives the reason (the thick, dense walls absorb heat by day and release it slowly at night) and connects it to the result (less need for heating and air conditioning).

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This explains how the walls are built, not why they save energy.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This mentions the energy benefit but gives no reason for it, and it puts the emphasis on the drawbacks.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This gives an example of a building that uses rammed earth but doesn't explain the energy savings.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Marine biologist Tavita Leota studies ways to restore damaged coral reefs.
• She wanted to know whether corals grown in underwater nurseries survive heat waves as well as wild corals do.
• Her team grew coral fragments in an underwater nursery for 18 months.
• They then transplanted 400 of the fragments onto a damaged reef.
• After a 2023 heat wave, 62% of the transplanted fragments survived, compared with 58% of nearby wild corals.

content.stem: The student wants to present the aim and method of Leota's study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To learn whether nursery-grown corals survive heat waves as well as wild corals, Leota's team grew coral fragments in an underwater nursery for 18 months and then transplanted 400 of them onto a damaged reef.

choices.label: B
choices.text: After a 2023 heat wave, 62% of Leota's transplanted coral fragments survived, compared with 58% of nearby wild corals.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Leota, a marine biologist who studies reef restoration, wanted to know whether nursery-grown corals survive heat waves as well as wild corals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Leota's team transplanted 400 coral fragments that had been grown in an underwater nursery onto a damaged reef.

content.explanation: The goal has two parts: the aim (what Leota wanted to find out) and the method (what her team did). Choice A gives the aim in its opening phrase and then describes how the corals were grown and transplanted.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This reports the study's results, not its aim or method.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This gives the aim but not the method.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This gives part of the method but not the aim.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most bees forage only during daylight.
• Researchers had assumed that a sand bee species native to coastal deserts also foraged only in daylight.
• In 2024, ecologist Ruth Okonjo placed infrared cameras near the bees' nests.
• The cameras recorded the bees leaving their nests to forage on moonlit nights.
• Night foraging was most common after days when temperatures rose above 40°C.
• Okonjo suggests that foraging at night helps the bees avoid extreme heat.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize that Okonjo's finding contradicted an earlier assumption. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Okonjo's cameras showed that the sand bees foraged at night most often after days above 40°C, suggesting that night foraging helps them avoid extreme heat.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most bees forage only in daylight, but Okonjo suggests that foraging at night may help some bees avoid extreme heat.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Although researchers had assumed that the sand bee foraged only in daylight, as most bees do, Okonjo's infrared cameras recorded the bees foraging on moonlit nights.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2024, Okonjo placed infrared cameras near the nests of a sand bee species native to coastal deserts.

content.explanation: To show a finding contradicted an assumption, the sentence must state both the assumption and the finding that overturned it. Choice C does: researchers assumed the sand bee foraged only by day, but Okonjo's cameras caught it foraging at night. "Although" marks the contradiction.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This explains when and why the bees forage at night, but it never mentions what researchers had assumed.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This contrasts most bees with Okonjo's explanation, but it doesn't state the earlier assumption about this species or that the cameras actually recorded night foraging.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes the method only; it gives neither the assumption nor the finding.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Amara Selden was a novelist known for books set in small fishing towns.
• Her first novel, The Salt Ledger (1962), follows a family that runs a harbor shop.
• Her last novel, Low Tide at Mirrow (1998), is narrated by a retired lighthouse keeper.
• Low Tide at Mirrow is told entirely through the keeper's logbook entries.
• Critics have called Low Tide at Mirrow Selden's most experimental book.

content.stem: The student wants to introduce Low Tide at Mirrow to an audience already familiar with Amara Selden and her work. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Amara Selden, a novelist known for books set in small fishing towns, published Low Tide at Mirrow in 1998.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Selden's last novel, Low Tide at Mirrow (1998), is told entirely through the logbook entries of a retired lighthouse keeper, a form that has led critics to call it her most experimental book.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Selden's first novel, The Salt Ledger (1962), follows a family that runs a harbor shop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Novelist Amara Selden, whose last book was narrated by a retired lighthouse keeper, is known for books set in small fishing towns.

content.explanation: Readers who already know Selden don't need to be told who she is; they need to learn about this particular novel. Choice B refers to her simply as "Selden" and spends the sentence on the novel itself: when it appeared, how it is told, and why critics call it experimental.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This spends much of the sentence explaining who Selden is, which suits readers who don't know her, and it says little about the novel beyond its date.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This introduces a different novel, The Salt Ledger.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This sentence is mainly an introduction to Selden herself, which this audience doesn't need, and it doesn't even name Low Tide at Mirrow.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Many animals can sense Earth's magnetic field.
• Young loggerhead sea turtles use magnetic cues to stay on course during their long migrations in the Atlantic Ocean.
• Homing pigeons rely partly on Earth's magnetic field to find their way home.
• Some salmon appear to use magnetic cues to return to the river where they hatched.
• Scientists are still debating exactly how animals detect magnetic fields.

content.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about how animals use their ability to sense Earth's magnetic field. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Young loggerhead sea turtles use magnetic cues during their migrations in the Atlantic Ocean, and homing pigeons rely partly on Earth's magnetic field to find their way home.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Scientists are still debating exactly how animals such as sea turtles, pigeons, and salmon detect Earth's magnetic field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Many animals can sense Earth's magnetic field.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A range of animals, from sea turtles to pigeons to salmon, use Earth's magnetic field to help them find their way.

content.explanation: A generalization makes a broad statement that covers many cases. The goal is a generalization about how animals use the magnetic sense. Choice D makes a broad claim (a range of animals use the field to find their way) and backs it with the examples from the notes.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This lists two specific examples but never draws the general conclusion they point to.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This is general, but it is about how animals detect the field, not how they use it.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This is general, but it says only that animals can sense the field, not how they use that ability.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Alder Creek Seed Library lends vegetable and flower seeds to local gardeners for free.
• It was founded in 2016 inside the public library in the town of Alder Creek.
• Borrowers plant the seeds, let some plants go to seed, and return new seeds at the end of the season.
• Librarian Marisol Ortega started the program with seeds donated by twelve local gardeners.
• The seed library now offers more than 200 varieties.

content.stem: The student wants to indicate when and where the seed library was founded. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Alder Creek Seed Library was founded in 2016 inside the public library in the town of Alder Creek.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Librarian Marisol Ortega started the Alder Creek Seed Library with seeds donated by twelve local gardeners.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Alder Creek Seed Library, which lends seeds to local gardeners for free, now offers more than 200 varieties.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Borrowers from the Alder Creek Seed Library return new seeds at the end of the season.

content.explanation: The goal asks for two facts: when the seed library was founded and where. Choice A gives both: it was founded in 2016 (when) inside the public library in Alder Creek (where).

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This says who started the seed library and with what seeds, but not when or where it was founded.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This describes what the seed library does and how many varieties it has now, with no founding date or location.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This explains how borrowers return seeds, which says nothing about when or where the seed library was founded.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Shield volcanoes and stratovolcanoes are two common types of volcanoes.
• Shield volcanoes are built mostly from runny lava that flows long distances before hardening.
• As a result, shield volcanoes are broad with gentle slopes.
• Stratovolcanoes are built from alternating layers of thick, sticky lava, ash, and rock fragments.
• These materials pile up near the vent, giving stratovolcanoes steep sides.
• Mauna Loa in Hawaii is a shield volcano; Mount Fuji in Japan is a stratovolcano.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference in the shapes of the two types of volcanoes. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is a shield volcano, while Mount Fuji in Japan is a stratovolcano.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Shield volcanoes are built mostly from runny lava, while stratovolcanoes are built from layers of thick lava, ash, and rock fragments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shield volcanoes are broad with gentle slopes, whereas stratovolcanoes have steep sides.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Stratovolcanoes have steep sides because the thick lava, ash, and rock fragments that build them pile up near the vent.

content.explanation: The goal is to contrast the shapes of the two types. Choice C describes the shape of each (broad with gentle slopes versus steep sides) and uses "whereas" to set them against each other.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This names an example of each type but says nothing about their shapes.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This contrasts what the volcanoes are made of, not their shapes.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This explains the shape of only one type, so it doesn't present a difference between the two.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• An urban heat island is a city area that is noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside.
• Pavement and rooftops absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat at night.
• In 2025, researcher Daniel Okoro measured summer nighttime temperatures across the city of Westbrook.
• Neighborhoods with the fewest trees were up to 4°C warmer at night than nearby rural areas.
• Neighborhoods with the most trees were less than 1°C warmer than nearby rural areas.

content.stem: The student wants to present Okoro's findings to an audience unfamiliar with urban heat islands. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Okoro found that the Westbrook neighborhoods with the fewest trees formed the strongest urban heat islands, up to 4°C warmer at night than nearby rural areas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Okoro found that some Westbrook neighborhoods are urban heat islands, areas noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside: those with the fewest trees were up to 4°C warmer at night than nearby rural areas, while those with the most trees were less than 1°C warmer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: An urban heat island is a city area that is noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside, partly because pavement and rooftops absorb sunlight during the day and release the heat at night.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2025, Okoro measured summer nighttime temperatures across Westbrook to study urban heat islands.

content.explanation: The goal has two parts: present Okoro's findings, and do it for readers who don't know what an urban heat island is. Choice B explains the term ("areas noticeably warmer than the surrounding countryside") and then gives the findings, comparing neighborhoods with the fewest and the most trees.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This presents a finding but uses the term "urban heat islands" without explaining it, which would confuse an audience unfamiliar with it.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This explains the term well but leaves out Okoro's findings entirely.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes what Okoro measured, not what he found, and it doesn't explain the term.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Mary Anning (1799–1847) collected fossils along the coast near Lyme Regis, England.
• In 1811 and 1812, she and her brother Joseph uncovered the skull and skeleton of an ichthyosaur, an extinct marine reptile.
• In 1823, she found the first complete plesiosaur skeleton.
• Leading scientists of her time bought her fossils and relied on her knowledge.
• As a woman, she was not allowed to join the Geological Society of London.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize that Anning made important discoveries even though she was excluded from a leading scientific society. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Mary Anning, who lived from 1799 to 1847, collected fossils along the coast near Lyme Regis, England.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Leading scientists of Anning's time bought her fossils and relied on her knowledge.

choices.label: C
choices.text: As a woman, Mary Anning was not allowed to join the Geological Society of London.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Although as a woman she could not join the Geological Society of London, Mary Anning made major discoveries, including the first complete plesiosaur skeleton in 1823.

content.explanation: The goal pairs two ideas: Anning was excluded from a scientific society, yet she made important discoveries. Choice D includes both and links them with "although," which emphasizes that her achievements came despite the exclusion.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This gives background on Anning but mentions neither her discoveries nor her exclusion.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This shows that scientists valued her work but doesn't mention her exclusion from the Geological Society.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This states her exclusion but doesn't mention any of her discoveries.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Engineering student Priya Raman designed a device called the DripCheck.
• The DripCheck clips onto an outdoor water faucet.
• It measures how much water flows through the faucet each day.
• Its purpose is to alert homeowners to slow leaks that could raise their water bills.
• Raman built her first prototype in 2024 using parts that cost about \$15.

content.stem: The student wants to explain the purpose of the DripCheck. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Raman built the first DripCheck prototype in 2024 using parts that cost about \$15.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The DripCheck, designed by engineering student Priya Raman, clips onto an outdoor water faucet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The DripCheck measures daily water flow through an outdoor faucet in order to alert homeowners to slow leaks that could raise their water bills.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Engineering student Priya Raman designed a device that clips onto an outdoor water faucet.

content.explanation: A device's purpose is what it is meant to do. Choice C says the DripCheck measures water flow "in order to alert homeowners to slow leaks," which states its purpose directly.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This gives the date and cost of the prototype, not what the device is for.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This says who designed the device and where it attaches, but not what it is for.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes the device's designer and where it attaches, but not its purpose.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Psychologist Elena Varga studied whether background music affects how quickly people solve puzzles.
• She tested 30 university students, all of whom were music majors.
• Students solved puzzles faster with instrumental music playing than in silence.
• Students solved puzzles slowest when music with lyrics was playing.
• Varga notes that because all the participants were trained musicians, the results may not apply to people without musical training.

content.stem: The student wants to present one of Varga's results while acknowledging a limitation of her study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Varga found that students solved puzzles faster with instrumental music than in silence, though because all 30 participants were music majors, the result may not apply to people without musical training.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Varga tested 30 university students, all of them music majors, to learn whether background music affects how quickly people solve puzzles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students in Varga's study solved puzzles fastest with instrumental music and slowest with music that had lyrics.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Varga notes that her results may not apply to people without musical training.

content.explanation: The goal needs both a result and a limitation. Choice A gives a result (puzzles were solved faster with instrumental music than in silence) and then, with "though," acknowledges the limitation: all participants were music majors, so the result may not apply to everyone.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This describes who was tested and why but gives no result, and it doesn't point out that testing only music majors limits the findings.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This presents results but doesn't acknowledge any limitation.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This states the limitation but doesn't present any result.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In the hot summer of 1858, the sewage-filled River Thames in London smelled so bad that the period became known as the "Great Stink."
• The stench prompted Parliament to approve a new sewer system for the city.
• Engineer Joseph Bazalgette designed the system.
• It included about 132 kilometers of large main sewers that carried waste away from central London.
• Much of Bazalgette's system is still in use today.

content.stem: The student wants to explain what led to the construction of London's new sewer system. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: London's sewer system, designed by engineer Joseph Bazalgette, included about 132 kilometers of large main sewers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Much of the sewer system that Joseph Bazalgette designed for London is still in use today.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Joseph Bazalgette designed a sewer system that carried waste away from central London.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After the "Great Stink" of 1858, when the sewage-filled Thames smelled terribly in the summer heat, Parliament approved a new sewer system for London.

content.explanation: The goal is to explain the cause of the sewer system. Choice D names that cause, the "Great Stink" of 1858, and connects it to Parliament's approval of the new system.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This describes the system's size and designer but not what led to its construction.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This describes the system's lasting use today, not why it was built.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This says what the system did, but not what event led to it being built.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Teodora Vance is a muralist based in Tucson, Arizona.
• She is known for large outdoor murals that depict desert plants and animals.
• In 2023, she completed Night Bloom, a mural on the side of a city water tower.
• Night Bloom shows a saguaro cactus flowering under a full moon.
• Vance painted the mural with a reflective paint that glows faintly after dark.

content.stem: The student wants to introduce Night Bloom to an audience unfamiliar with Teodora Vance. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Night Bloom, which Vance completed in 2023, shows a saguaro cactus flowering under a full moon.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Teodora Vance, a Tucson-based muralist known for large outdoor murals of desert plants and animals, completed Night Bloom, a mural of a saguaro cactus flowering under a full moon, in 2023.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Teodora Vance is a Tucson-based muralist known for large outdoor murals of desert plants and animals.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vance painted Night Bloom on a city water tower using a reflective paint that glows faintly after dark.

content.explanation: Readers who don't know Vance need to learn who she is, and the goal also requires introducing Night Bloom. Choice B does both: it gives her full name and identifies her as a Tucson muralist known for desert scenes, and then describes the mural and when she completed it.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This introduces the mural but refers to "Vance" by last name only, without saying who she is, which assumes the audience already knows her.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This introduces Vance but never mentions Night Bloom.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This describes how the mural was painted but refers to "Vance" without any introduction, as if readers already knew her.

While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
• Jupiter's diameter is about 140,000 kilometers.
• Earth's diameter is about 12,700 kilometers.
• Jupiter's diameter is about 11 times Earth's.
• Jupiter is made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

content.stem: The student wants to emphasize how much larger Jupiter is than Earth. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: With a diameter of about 140,000 kilometers, Jupiter is roughly 11 times as wide as Earth.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Jupiter, the largest planet in our solar system, is made mostly of hydrogen and helium.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Earth's diameter is about 12,700 kilometers.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.

content.explanation: The goal is a comparison between Jupiter and Earth. Choice A gives Jupiter's diameter and says it is about 11 times as wide as Earth, which shows exactly how much larger it is.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This describes what Jupiter is made of and doesn't compare its size with Earth's.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This gives Earth's size alone, with nothing about Jupiter to compare it to.

distractorRationales.label: D
distractorRationales.text: This says Jupiter is the largest planet but doesn't compare it with Earth or show how much larger it is.

passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Washi is a traditional Japanese paper.
• It is often made from the inner bark of the kozo, or paper mulberry, shrub.
• Kozo fibers are much longer than the wood-pulp fibers used in most modern paper.
• Long fibers tangle tightly together, making the finished sheet strong and resistant to tearing.
• Washi has been used for books, scrolls, lanterns, and sliding doors.

content.stem: The student wants to explain why washi made from kozo resists tearing. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Washi, a traditional Japanese paper, has been used for books, scrolls, lanterns, and sliding doors.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Washi is often made from the inner bark of the kozo, or paper mulberry, shrub.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Unlike most modern paper, washi is a traditional Japanese paper that is often made from the inner bark of a shrub.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Because kozo fibers are much longer than the wood-pulp fibers in most modern paper, they tangle tightly together, making washi strong and resistant to tearing.

content.explanation: The goal asks why kozo washi resists tearing, so the answer needs a cause. Choice D gives it: kozo fibers are long, long fibers tangle tightly, and that tangling makes the paper strong. "Because" signals the explanation.

distractorRationales.label: A
distractorRationales.text: This lists uses of washi but doesn't explain why it resists tearing.

distractorRationales.label: B
distractorRationales.text: This names the material washi is made from but doesn't say why that material makes the paper strong.

distractorRationales.label: C
distractorRationales.text: This contrasts washi with modern paper but gives no reason it resists tearing.
